document: A genuine redundancy occurs when an employer no longer requires the employee's job to be performed by anyone because of operational changes, and the employer has complied with any consultation obligations. A dismissal is not a genuine redundancy if it would have been reasonable to redeploy the employee within the enterprise.
summary: A redundancy is genuine only when the job is no longer needed, consultation obligations are met and redeployment was not reasonable.

document: Single Touch Payroll requires employers to report salary or wages, pay as you go withholding and superannuation information to the tax office each time they pay employees. Employees can view their year-to-date information through their online government services account.
summary: Single Touch Payroll requires employers to report wages, withholding and super to the tax office each payday.

document: Modern awards set out minimum terms and conditions of employment for an industry or occupation, in addition to the National Employment Standards. They include minimum wages, penalty rates, overtime, allowances, rostering arrangements and consultation obligations. The Fair Work Commission reviews modern awards and may vary them.
summary: Modern awards set minimum pay and conditions for an industry or occupation on top of the National Employment Standards and are reviewed by the Fair Work Commission.

document: The whistleblower provisions in Part 9.4AAA of the Corporations Act protect eligible whistleblowers who disclose misconduct or an improper state of affairs concerning a regulated entity. Disclosures can be made to ASIC, APRA, an eligible recipient within the entity, or a legal practitioner. Public companies, large proprietary companies and trustees of registrable superannuation entities must have a whistleblower policy. Victimising a whistleblower is a civil penalty provision and a criminal offence.
summary: The Corporations Act protects whistleblowers who report misconduct and requires larger companies to have a whistleblower policy.

document: The Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre regulates reporting entities that provide designated services. Reporting entities must enrol, maintain an anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing program, verify customer identity and report suspicious matters, threshold transactions and international funds transfer instructions.
summary: AUSTRAC requires reporting entities to run anti-money laundering programs, verify customers and report suspicious and threshold transactions.

document: Section 588G of the Corporations Act imposes a duty on directors to prevent a company from incurring a debt when there are reasonable grounds to suspect the company is insolvent. A director who breaches the duty may face civil penalties and be ordered to compensate the company for creditor losses. The safe harbour provisions in section 588GA can protect a director who develops a course of action reasonably likely to lead to a better outcome for the company than immediate administration or liquidation.
summary: Directors must not let a company incur debts while insolvent, although safe harbour can protect those pursuing a better outcome.

document: Liquidation is the process of winding up a company's affairs, realising its assets and distributing the proceeds to creditors in the statutory order of priority. Employee entitlements such as wages, superannuation, leave and redundancy pay are generally paid ahead of ordinary unsecured creditors.
summary: Liquidation winds up a company and distributes asset proceeds to creditors by statutory priority, with employee entitlements paid before unsecured creditors.

document: The superannuation guarantee requires employers to contribute a minimum percentage of an eligible employee's ordinary time earnings to a complying superannuation fund. The rate rose to 11.5 percent on 1 July 2024 and to 12 percent on 1 July 2025. Contributions must be paid at least four times a year, by the 28th day after the end of each quarter. Employers who miss a quarterly deadline must lodge a superannuation guarantee charge statement and pay the charge, which includes the shortfall, nominal interest and an administration fee.
summary: Employers must pay at least 12 percent super quarterly, and missed deadlines trigger the superannuation guarantee charge.

document: A public company must hold an annual general meeting at least once each calendar year and within five months after the end of its financial year. The business of the meeting usually includes considering the financial report, the directors' report and the auditor's report, electing directors and appointing the auditor. Listed companies must also put a non-binding resolution to adopt the remuneration report. If 25 percent or more of votes are cast against the report at two consecutive meetings, a spill resolution must be put to members.
summary: Public companies must hold an AGM within five months of year end, and listed companies vote on the remuneration report.

document: Every company director must have a director identification number, a unique 15-digit identifier that a director keeps permanently. Applications are made to the Australian Business Registry Services and must be completed personally by the director because identity verification is required. Newly appointed directors must apply before their appointment. Failing to hold a director identification number when required can attract civil and criminal penalties.
summary: Every director needs a permanent 15-digit director ID, applied for personally through the Australian Business Registry Services before appointment.

document: A company must keep written financial records that correctly record and explain its transactions and financial position and performance, and would enable true and fair financial statements to be prepared and audited. The records must be retained for seven years after the transactions covered by the records are completed.
summary: Companies must keep financial records that explain their transactions and allow audited statements to be prepared, and retain them for seven years.

document: Directors and other officers must exercise their powers and discharge their duties with the degree of care and diligence that a reasonable person would exercise if they were a director or officer of a corporation in the corporation's circumstances and occupied the same office.
summary: Directors and officers must act with the care and diligence of a reasonable person in their position.

document: Voluntary administration begins when a company's directors appoint an independent administrator because they believe the company is or is likely to become insolvent. The administrator investigates the company's affairs and holds a first meeting of creditors within eight business days. At the second meeting, creditors decide whether the company should execute a deed of company arrangement, go into liquidation, or be returned to the directors. During the administration a moratorium generally prevents creditors from enforcing their claims.
summary: Directors of an insolvent company can appoint an administrator, and creditors later decide the company's future while a moratorium applies.

document: Entities listed on the Australian Securities Exchange must immediately disclose information that a reasonable person would expect to have a material effect on the price or value of their securities. Listing Rule 3.1 sets out the obligation, and section 674 of the Corporations Act gives it statutory force. Limited exceptions apply where the information is confidential, a reasonable person would not expect it to be disclosed, and it concerns an incomplete proposal or is a trade secret. ASIC may issue infringement notices for suspected breaches.
summary: Listed entities must immediately disclose price-sensitive information unless a narrow confidentiality exception applies.

document: A general deduction is available for a loss or outgoing to the extent it is incurred in gaining or producing assessable income, or is necessarily incurred in carrying on a business for that purpose. Outgoings of a capital, private or domestic nature are not deductible under the general provision.
summary: Outgoings are deductible when incurred in earning assessable income or running a business, but not if they are capital, private or domestic.

document: The Commissioner of Taxation has general administration of the income tax law and may issue public rulings that bind the Commissioner when they apply to a taxpayer. A taxpayer who relies on a public ruling is protected from shortfall penalties and interest if the ruling is later found to be incorrect.
summary: Public rulings issued by the Commissioner bind the Commissioner and protect taxpayers who rely on them from penalties and interest.

document: Payroll tax is a state and territory tax on wages paid or payable by an employer to its employees once total Australian wages exceed a threshold. Each jurisdiction sets its own rate and threshold, and grouping provisions combine the wages of related businesses when testing the threshold. Taxable wages commonly include salaries, superannuation contributions, fringe benefits and certain contractor payments. Employers register with the revenue office in each state where they pay wages and lodge periodic returns.
summary: Payroll tax is a state tax on wages above a threshold, with grouping rules and registration in each state where wages are paid.

document: The general protections provisions protect workplace rights, freedom of association and freedom from discrimination. A person must not take adverse action against another person because they have a workplace right, have exercised a workplace right, or propose to exercise a workplace right.
summary: General protections stop anyone taking adverse action against a person for having or exercising a workplace right.

document: The financial reporting requirements in Chapter 2M of the Corporations Act apply to disclosing entities, public companies, large proprietary companies and registered schemes. Financial reports must comply with accounting standards and must be audited unless relief is available.
summary: Public companies, large proprietary companies, disclosing entities and registered schemes must prepare audited financial reports that meet accounting standards.

document: The superannuation guarantee charge is not deductible, unlike superannuation contributions paid on time. Employers that do not pay the charge may be issued a director penalty notice, making directors personally liable for the unpaid amount.
summary: Late superannuation guarantee charges are not deductible and unpaid amounts can make directors personally liable.

document: A trust is an obligation imposed on a trustee to deal with property for the benefit of beneficiaries. Discretionary trusts give the trustee discretion to decide which beneficiaries receive distributions of income or capital in each income year.
summary: A trustee holds property for beneficiaries and, in a discretionary trust, decides who receives income or capital each year.

document: The National Employment Standards are eleven minimum entitlements that apply to all employees covered by the national workplace relations system. They cover maximum weekly hours, requests for flexible working arrangements, parental leave, annual leave, personal leave, community service leave, long service leave, public holidays, notice of termination and redundancy pay, the Fair Work Information Statement and offers to convert casual employment.
summary: The National Employment Standards set eleven minimum entitlements for national system employees, covering hours, leave, notice and redundancy.

document: Persons conducting a business or undertaking have a primary duty to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety of workers engaged or caused to be engaged by them. Officers must exercise due diligence to ensure the business complies with its duties.
summary: Businesses must ensure worker health and safety so far as reasonably practicable, and officers must exercise due diligence.

document: A company is a separate legal entity with the capacity and powers of an individual and of a body corporate. It can own property, enter contracts and sue or be sued in its own name. Members of a company limited by shares are liable only for any amount unpaid on their shares.
summary: A company is a separate legal entity that can own property and contract, and shareholders are liable only for unpaid amounts on their shares.

document: A director must exercise their powers and discharge their duties in good faith in the best interests of the corporation and for a proper purpose. A person who is involved in a contravention of these duties may also contravene the law as an accessory.
summary: Directors must act in good faith in the company's best interests and for a proper purpose, and accessories to breaches can also be liable.

document: Assessable income includes ordinary income, such as salary, wages, business income and interest, together with statutory income that is specifically included by a provision of the income tax law. Exempt income and non-assessable non-exempt income are excluded when calculating taxable income.
summary: Assessable income covers ordinary and statutory income, while exempt and non-assessable non-exempt income are excluded from taxable income.

document: Division 7A treats certain payments, loans and forgiven debts provided by a private company to shareholders or their associates as unfranked dividends unless the loan is placed on complying terms before the company's lodgment day.
summary: Division 7A treats private company payments, loans and forgiven debts to shareholders as unfranked dividends unless loans are put on complying terms.
